headline: Generative models co-design sequence and structure for peptides, antibodies, and ligands
label: Generative Ai Biomolecular Design
summary: Recent preprints and papers apply flow matching, energy guidance, and interpretable architectures to peptide, antibody, and ligand design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is structure- or target-conditioned generative modeling of biomolecules. Flow-matching approaches appear in ForceFlowAb, which adds differentiable force-field guidance to antigen-conditioned CDR co-design, and in Ourotide, which uses conditional geometric flow matching with interface-aware affinity learning for peptides. LDDM extends 3D generation to docking, fragment linking, and de novo design with synthesizability control, while PockLigGPT conditions molecule generation on pocket sequences and applies docking-guided reinforcement learning. Proteina-Complexa codesigns sequence and structure for binders to polar epitopes. Newer elements include interpretability, as in LAMINA, whose motif-level peptide-HLA scoring learns binding energetics and structure, and energy rank alignment for few-shot directed evolution. SAbR addresses structure-only antibody renumbering, a supporting tool rather than a design method.
